4. Past-paper question bank






注记



2019 Paper 1 中检出的矩阵题属于旧考纲的 eigenvalues、diagonalisation 或四维变换，因此不收入本节。以下题目按完全相同的地区版本合并，答案依据对应的 Cambridge mark scheme 整理。



2020



2020 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 6 · 13 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) The transformation represented by \(A^{-1}\) maps a triangle of area \(30\text{ cm}^2\) to a triangle of area \(d\text{ cm}^2\). Find \(d\). [3]
(b) Prove by induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
A^n=\begin{pmatrix}2^n&0\\2^n-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
[5]
Let \(B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\33&0\end{pmatrix}\).
(c) The line \(y=2x\) is invariant under the transformation represented by \(A^nB\). Find \(n\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Since
\[
\det A=2,\qquad \det(A^{-1})=(\det A)^{-1}=\frac12,
\]
the area scale factor is \(\left|\det(A^{-1})\right|=\frac12\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{d=30\times\frac12=15}.
\]
(b) For \(n=1\),
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}2^1&0\\2^1-1&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
so the statement is true initially. Assume that it is true for \(n=k\), where \(k\) is a positive integer:
\[
A^k=\begin{pmatrix}2^k&0\\2^k-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
A^{k+1}=\begin{pmatrix}2^k&0\\2^k-1&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}2^{k+1}&0\\2^{k+1}-1&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
Thus the statement is true for \(k+1\) whenever it is true for \(k\). Hence, by mathematical induction,
\[
\boxed{A^n=\begin{pmatrix}2^n&0\\2^n-1&1\end{pmatrix}}
\]
for every positive integer \(n\).
(c) Using part (b),
\[
A^nB=\begin{pmatrix}2^n&0\\2^n+32&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For a general point \((x,y)\),
\[
A^nB\binom xy
=\binom{2^nx}{(2^n+32)x}.
\]
The image has gradient \((2^n+32)/2^n\). Since the invariant line has gradient \(2\),
\[
\frac{2^n+32}{2^n}=2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
2^n=32
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{n=5}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2020, Q6; 9231/12/M/J/2020, Q6.





2020 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 4 · 11 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}k&0&2\\0&-1&-1\\1&1&-k\end{pmatrix},\quad
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&-3\\-1&3\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\begin{pmatrix}-3&-1&1\\1&1&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Show that \(A\) is non-singular. [3]
It is given that
\[
CAB=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-\frac32\\-1&-\frac32\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Find \(k\). [3]
(c) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(CAB\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Expanding along the first row,
\[
\det A
=k\begin{vmatrix}-1&-1\\1&-k\end{vmatrix}
+2\begin{vmatrix}0&-1\\1&1\end{vmatrix}
=k(k+1)+2
=k^2+k+2.
\]
The discriminant of \(k^2+k+2\) is
\[
1^2-4(1)(2)=-7<0.
\]
Since its leading coefficient is positive, \(k^2+k+2>0\) for every real \(k\). Thus \(\det A\ne0\) and \(A\) is non-singular.
(b) First,
\[
AB=\begin{pmatrix}0&-3k\\1&-3\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
and hence
\[
CAB
=\begin{pmatrix}-2&9k+3\\-1&-3k-3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Comparing, for example, the top-right entry with the given matrix,
\[
9k+3=-\frac32
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{k=-\frac12}.
\]
(c) The given \(CAB\) maps a point \((x,y)\) to
\[
\binom XY
=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-\frac32\\-1&-\frac32\end{pmatrix}
\binom xy
=\binom{-2x-\frac32y}{-x-\frac32y}.
\]
For the line \(y=mx\), substitute \(y=mx\) and require \(Y=mX\):
\[
-1-\frac32m=m\left(-2-\frac32m\right),
\]
Thus
\[
3m^2+m-2=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(3m-2)(m+1)=0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{y=\frac23x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-x}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2020, Q4.





2020 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 1 · 9 marks
Let
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(a,b>0\).
(a) State the two transformations represented by \(M\), in the correct order. [2]
The unit square is mapped by \(M\) onto parallelogram \(OPQR\).
(b) Find the matrix mapping \(OPQR\) back onto the unit square. [2]
(c) Given that the area of \(OPQR\) is \(2\text{ cm}^2\) and \(x+3y=0\) is invariant, find \(a\) and \(b\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Reading the product from right to left, first apply a one-way stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis with scale factor \(a\), then a shear with the \(x\)-axis fixed, taking \((0,1)\) to \((b,1)\).
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Since \(\det M=a\),
\[
\boxed{M^{-1}=\frac1a\begin{pmatrix}1&-b\\0&a\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(c) The unit square has area \(1\), so its image has area
\[
|\det M|=a.
\]
As \(a>0\) and the given area is \(2\), \(\boxed{a=2}\). A general point on \(x+3y=0\) can be written as \((x,-x/3)\). Its image is
\[
\binom XY
=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\binom{x}{-x/3}
=\binom{ax-\frac13bx}{-\frac13x}.
\]
The image must again satisfy \(X+3Y=0\):
\[
ax-\frac13bx-x=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
1=a-\frac b3.
\]
Using \(a=2\) gives \(\boxed{b=3}\), so \(\boxed{a=2, b=3}\).

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2020, Q1; 9231/13/O/N/2020, Q1.





2020 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 4 · 13 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B=\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Identify the transformation represented by \(A\). [1]
(b) Identify the transformation represented by \(B\). [2]
Triangle \(DEF\) is transformed by \(AB\) onto triangle \(PQR\).
(c) Show that the two triangles have the same area. [3]
(d) Find the matrix mapping \(PQR\) onto \(DEF\). [2]
(e) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(AB\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) \(A\) represents reflection in the line \(y=x\).
(b) Comparing \(B\) with the standard rotation matrix shows that it represents a rotation through \(60^\circ\) anticlockwise about the origin.
(c) Multiplying in the stated order,
\[
AB=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\\[2pt]\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det(AB)=-1,
\]
Therefore the area scale factor is \(|\det(AB)|=1\), so triangles \(DEF\) and \(PQR\) have equal area.
(d) Using the \(2\times2\) inverse formula,
\[
\boxed{(AB)^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\\[2pt]\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(e) Under \(AB\),
\[
\binom XY
=\binom{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}x+\frac12y}{\frac12x-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}y}.
\]
Put \(y=mx\) and require \(Y=mX\):
\[
\frac12-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}m
=m\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\frac12m\right).
\]
Hence
\[
m^2+2\sqrt3m-1=0,
\]
so \(m=-\sqrt3\pm2\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{y=(2-\sqrt3)x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-(2+\sqrt3)x}.
\]


      xy O    y = (2 − √3)x y = −(2 + √3)x


2020 O/N 12 Q4: the two invariant directions are perpendicular, as expected for a reflection.



 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/12/O/N/2020, Q4.




2021



2021 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 4 · 14 marks
A rotation of \(60^\circ\) anticlockwise about the origin is followed by a one-way stretch in the \(x\)-direction with scale factor \(d\), where \(d\ne0\).
(a) Find the matrix \(M\) of the combined transformation. [4]
(b) The unit square is mapped by \(M\) onto a parallelogram of area \(\frac12d^2\). Show that \(d=2\). [2]
Let \(N\) satisfy
\[
MN=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\[2pt]\frac12&\frac12\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(c) Find \(N\). [3]
(d) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(MN\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) The rotation matrix is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix},
\]
and the following stretch has matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}d&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\). Hence, in the correct order,
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}d&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}\frac d2&-\frac{d\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Since
\[
\det M=\frac d4+\frac{3d}{4}=d,
\]
the image area is \(|d|\). In the geometrical stretch context \(d>0\), so
\[
d=\frac12d^2.
\]
As \(d\ne0\), \(\boxed{d=2}\).
(c) With \(d=2\),
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&-\sqrt3\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
M^{-1}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&\sqrt3\\[2pt]-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore
\[
N=M^{-1}(MN)
=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&\sqrt3\\[2pt]-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\[2pt]\frac12&\frac12\end{pmatrix}
\]
and hence
\[
\boxed{N=\frac14\begin{pmatrix}1+\sqrt3&1+\sqrt3\\1-\sqrt3&1-\sqrt3\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(d) Under \(MN\),
\[
\binom XY
=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\[2pt]\frac12&\frac12\end{pmatrix}
\binom xy
=\binom{x+y}{\frac12x+\frac12y}.
\]
For \(y=mx\), the condition \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
\frac12+\frac12m=m(1+m)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
2m^2+m-1=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(2m-1)(m+1)=0.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{y=\frac12x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-x}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2021, Q4; 9231/12/M/J/2021, Q4.





2021 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 4 · 11 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&k&k\\5&-1&3\\1&0&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&1\\-1&2&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Find \(CAB\). [3]
(b) Given that \(A\) is singular, find \(k\). [3]
(c) Using this value of \(k\), find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(CAB\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) First,
\[
AB=\begin{pmatrix}2+k&k\\8&-1\\2&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
so
\[
CAB
=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&1\\-1&2&0\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}2+k&k\\8&-1\\2&0\end{pmatrix}
=\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}10&-1\\14-k&-k-2\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(b) Expanding \(\det A\) along the first row,
\[
\det A
=2\begin{vmatrix}-1&3\\0&1\end{vmatrix}
-k\begin{vmatrix}5&3\\1&1\end{vmatrix}
+k\begin{vmatrix}5&-1\\1&0\end{vmatrix}
=-2-k.
\]
Since \(A\) is singular, \(-2-k=0\), giving \(\boxed{k=-2}\).
(c) Hence
\[
CAB=\begin{pmatrix}10&-1\\16&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
which maps \((x,mx)\) to \((10x-mx,16x)\). Requiring \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
16=m(10-m),
\]
so \(m^2-10m+16=0\). Therefore \(\boxed{y=2x}\) or \(\boxed{y=8x}\).

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2021, Q4.





2021 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 4 · 11 marks
Let
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) State the two transformations represented by \(M\), in the correct order. [2]
(b) For \(0\le\theta\le\pi\), find the values of \(\theta\) for which the transformation has exactly one invariant line through the origin. [9]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Reading the product from right to left, first apply a one-way stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis with scale factor \(3\), then rotate anticlockwise through \(\theta\) about the origin.
(b) Multiplying gives
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}3\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\3\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For a point \((x,mx)\),
\[
X=(3\cos\theta-m\sin\theta)x,
\qquad
Y=(3\sin\theta+m\cos\theta)x.
\]
Requiring \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
3\sin\theta+m\cos\theta
=3m\cos\theta-m^2\sin\theta,
\]
which reduces to
\[
m^2\sin\theta-2m\cos\theta+3\sin\theta=0.
\]
Exactly one finite-gradient invariant line requires a repeated root, so the discriminant must be zero:
\[
4\cos^2\theta-12\sin^2\theta=0.
\]
Thus \(\tan^2\theta=1/3\). In the stated interval this gives
\[
\boxed{\theta=\frac\pi6\text{ or }\frac{5\pi}6}.
\]
At the endpoints \(\theta=0,\pi\), both coordinate axes are invariant, so neither endpoint satisfies “exactly one”.

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2021, Q4; 9231/13/O/N/2021, Q4.





2021 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 1 · 9 marks
(a) Describe the transformation represented by \(\begin{pmatrix}6&0\\0&6\end{pmatrix}\). [1]
Let \(A=\begin{pmatrix}3&4\\2&2\end{pmatrix}\).
(b) A triangle of area \(13\text{ cm}^2\) is transformed by \(A\). Find the area of its image. [2]
(c) Find \(B\) such that \(AB=\begin{pmatrix}6&0\\0&6\end{pmatrix}\). [2]
(d) Show that the origin is the only invariant point of the transformation represented by \(A\). [4]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) The matrix \(6I\) represents an enlargement with centre the origin and scale factor \(6\).
(b)
\[
\det A=3(2)-4(2)=-2.
\]
Hence the area scale factor is \(|-2|=2\), and the image area is
\[
\boxed{2\times13=26\text{ cm}^2}.
\]
(c) Since \(AB=6I\),
\[
B=A^{-1}(6I)=6A^{-1}.
\]
Now
\[
A^{-1}=-\frac12\begin{pmatrix}2&-4\\-2&3\end{pmatrix},
\]
so
\[
\boxed{B=6A^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}-6&12\\6&-9\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(d) If \((x,y)\) is invariant, then
\[
\begin{pmatrix}3&4\\2&2\end{pmatrix}\binom xy=\binom xy.
\]
Thus
\[
3x+4y=x,\qquad 2x+2y=y,
\]
or
\[
2x+4y=0,\qquad 2x+y=0.
\]
The second equation gives \(y=-2x\); substituting into the first gives \(-6x=0\). Hence \(x=0\) and \(y=0\), so the origin is the only invariant point.

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/12/O/N/2021, Q1.




2022



2022 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 7 · 17 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\4&k&6\\7&8&9\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Find the set of values of \(k\) for which \(A\) is non-singular. [3]
(b) Given that \(A\) is non-singular, find the entries in the top row of \(A^{-1}\). [4]
Let \(B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}\).
(c) Give an example of a matrix \(C\) such that
\[
BAC=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\k&4\end{pmatrix}.
\]
[4]
(d) Find the set of values of \(k\) for which the transformation represented by \(\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\k&4\end{pmatrix}\) has two distinct invariant lines through the origin. [6]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Expanding along the first row,
\[
\det A
=1\begin{vmatrix}k&6\\8&9\end{vmatrix}
-2\begin{vmatrix}4&6\\7&9\end{vmatrix}
+3\begin{vmatrix}4&k\\7&8\end{vmatrix}
\]
\[
=(9k-48)-2(36-42)+3(32-7k)
=60-12k.
\]
Thus \(A\) is non-singular when
\[
\boxed{k\ne5}.
\]
(b) The top row of \(A^{-1}=(\det A)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}A\) is formed from the cofactors of the first column:
\[
(A^{-1})_{11}=\frac{\begin{vmatrix}k&6\\8&9\end{vmatrix}}{60-12k}
=\frac{3k-16}{4(5-k)},
\]
\[
(A^{-1})_{12}=\frac{-\begin{vmatrix}2&3\\8&9\end{vmatrix}}{60-12k}
=\frac1{2(5-k)},
\]
\[
(A^{-1})_{13}=\frac{\begin{vmatrix}2&3\\k&6\end{vmatrix}}{60-12k}
=\frac{4-k}{4(5-k)}.
\]
Therefore the top row is
\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{3k-16}{4(5-k)},\ \frac1{2(5-k)},\ \frac{4-k}{4(5-k)}\right)}.
\]
(c) Since
\[
BA=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\4&k&6\end{pmatrix},
\]
one valid choice is
\[
\boxed{C=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Indeed,
\[
BAC
=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\4&k&6\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\k&4\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(d) Let \(T=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\k&4\end{pmatrix}\). Then
\[
T\binom{x}{mx}=\binom{(2+m)x}{(k+4m)x}.
\]
For \(y=mx\) to be invariant, \(Y=mX\):
\[
k+4m=m(2+m),
\]
giving
\[
m^2-2m-k=0.
\]
Two distinct invariant lines require
\[
\Delta=(-2)^2-4(1)(-k)=4+4k>0,
\]
so \(k>-1\). Also \(T\) must be non-singular:
\[
\det T=8-k\ne0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{k>-1,\qquad k\ne8}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2022, Q7; 9231/12/M/J/2022, Q7.





2022 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 5 · 12 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(a>0\).
(a) State the type of transformation represented by \(A\). [1]
(b) Prove by induction that
\[
A^n=\begin{pmatrix}1&na\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\]
for every positive integer \(n\). [5]
Let
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}b&b\\1/a&1/a\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(b>0\).
(c) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(A^nB\). [6]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) \(A\) represents a shear in the \(x\)-direction, with the \(x\)-axis fixed and \((0,1)\) mapped to \((a,1)\).
(b) For \(n=1\), the stated formula is exactly the given matrix \(A\). Assume that it holds for \(n=k\):
\[
A^{k+1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&ka\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1&(k+1)a\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore the statement holds for \(k+1\) whenever it holds for \(k\). Hence, by mathematical induction, it is true for every positive integer \(n\).
(c) Using the result from part (b),
\[
A^nB=\begin{pmatrix}b+n&b+n\\1/a&1/a\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus
\[
\binom XY
=\binom{(b+n)(x+y)}{(x+y)/a}.
\]
For \(y=mx\), require \(Y=mX\):
\[
\frac{1+m}{a}=m(b+n)(1+m).
\]
Hence
\[
(1+m)\left\{\frac1a-m(b+n)\right\}=0,

=\cos\frac\pi4\cos\frac\pi6
+\sin\frac\pi4\sin\frac\pi6
=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4},
\]
and
\[
\sin\frac\pi{12}
=\sin\frac\pi4\cos\frac\pi6
-\cos\frac\pi4\sin\frac\pi6
=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}.
\]
(b) The matrix factorises as
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\pi/12)&-\sin(\pi/12)\\\sin(\pi/12)&\cos(\pi/12)\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Reading from right to left, first reflect in the \(x\)-axis, then rotate anticlockwise through \(\pi/12\) about the origin.
(c) Reversing the order and inverting each factor gives
\[
\boxed{M^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\pi/12)&\sin(\pi/12)\\-\sin(\pi/12)&\cos(\pi/12)\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(d) Write \(s=\sin(\pi/12)\) and \(c=\cos(\pi/12)\). A point \((x,mx)\) maps to
\[
\binom XY=\binom{(c+ms)x}{(s-mc)x}.
\]
The condition \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
s-mc=m(c+ms),
\]
so
\[
m^2s+2mc-s=0,
\]
as required. By the quadratic formula,
\[
m=\frac{-2c\pm\sqrt{4c^2+4s^2}}{2s}
=\frac{-c\pm1}{s}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{m=-\cot\frac\pi{12}\pm\cosec\frac\pi{12}}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/14/O/N/2025, Q5.

title: 1.4 Matrices
text:
5. 完成本节的判断标准

所有矩阵运算先检查阶数和乘法顺序；
能在无计算器条件下求 \(2\times2\)、\(3\times3\) 行列式和逆矩阵；
能从几何描述写出矩阵，也能从矩阵描述变换；
能正确组合多个变换并解释逆变换顺序；
能求不动点、不变直线和面积伸缩因子。

title: 1.6 Vectors
text:
重要本节考纲要求



考生需要能够：

使用并互相转换平面的 Cartesian、normal 与 parametric vector forms；
计算 vector product，并理解其方向和大小；
判断直线与平面相交、平行或直线位于平面内，并求交点；
求点到平面的垂足及距离；
求直线与平面、两个平面之间的角；
求两个平面的交线；
求两条 skew lines 的最短距离及 common perpendicular 的方程。

title: 1.6 Vectors
text:
学习路线


能从平面方程立即读出 normal vector
能在点、方向向量与 normal vector 之间选择合适的平面形式
能用 scalar product 判断平行、垂直和计算角度
能用 vector product 求共同垂直方向、平面 normal 和面积
能通过参数代入求 line-plane intersection
能建立 perpendicular line 求 foot of perpendicular
能求 two-plane intersection、skew-line distance 和 common perpendicular

title: 1.6 Vectors
text:
1. 教材知识点

1.1 Equations of a plane
过点 \(A\)，位置向量为 \(\mathbf a\)，并包含两个不平行方向 \(\mathbf b,\mathbf c\) 的平面可写成
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf b+\mu\mathbf c}.
\]
若 \(\mathbf n\) 是平面的 normal vector，则
\[
(\mathbf r-\mathbf a)\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=0,
\]
即
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=p},\;
p=\mathbf a\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n.
\]
若 \(\mathbf n=(a,b,c)\)，Cartesian form 为
\[
\boxed{ax+by+cz=d}.
\]
从 parametric form 转换时，可用 \(\mathbf b\times\mathbf c\) 求 normal；也可消去 \(\lambda,\mu\)。


1.2 A line and a plane
设直线
\[
\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf d
\]
和平面 \(\mathbf r\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=p\)。

若 \(\mathbf d\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n\ne0\)，直线与平面有唯一交点；
若 \(\mathbf d\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=0\)，直线平行于平面；
在平行情形下，若 \(\mathbf a\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=p\)，则整条直线位于平面内。

求交点时，把直线的 \(x,y,z\) 参数式代入平面方程，先求参数，再代回直线。


1.3 Foot of a perpendicular and distance to a plane
从点 \(P\) 到平面 \(\mathbf r\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=p\) 的垂线方向为 \(\mathbf n\)。先写
\[
\mathbf r=\mathbf p_0+t\mathbf n,
\]
再与平面联立，所得交点 \(M\) 是 foot of the perpendicular，距离为 \(|PM|\)。
对于平面 \(ax+by+cz=d\) 和点 \((x_0,y_0,z_0)\)，距离公式为
\[
\boxed{
D=\frac{|ax_0+by_0+cz_0-d|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}}
}.
\]


1.4 Angle between a line and a plane
若直线方向为 \(\mathbf d\)，平面 normal 为 \(\mathbf n\)，直线与平面的锐角为 \(\alpha\)，则
\[
\boxed{
\sin\alpha=\frac{|\mathbf d\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n|}{|\mathbf d|\,|\mathbf n|}
}.
\]
这里使用 \(\sin\alpha\)，因为直线与平面的角与 \(\mathbf d\)、\(\mathbf n\) 之间的角互余。


1.5 Intersection and angle of two planes
两个不平行平面的交集是一条直线。可用两种方法求交线：

令一个坐标为参数，联立两个 Cartesian equations；
取两平面的 normals \(\mathbf n_1,\mathbf n_2\)，则交线方向平行于 \[\mathbf n_1\times\mathbf n_2,\] 再求交线上的一个点。

两平面的锐角等于其 normals 的锐角：
\[
\boxed{
\cos\theta= rac{|\mathbf n_1\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n_2|}
{|\mathbf n_1|\,|\mathbf n_2|}
}.
\]
所有包含平面 \(\pi_1:f_1=0\) 与 \(\pi_2:f_2=0\) 的公共交线的平面可写成
\[
pf_1+qf_2=0,
\]
其中 \(p,q\) 不同时为零。


1.6 Vector product
对于
\[
\mathbf a=(a_1,a_2,a_3),\;
\mathbf b=(b_1,b_2,b_3),
\]
\[
\boxed{
\mathbf a\times\mathbf b=
\begin{pmatrix}
a_2b_3-a_3b_2\\
a_3b_1-a_1b_3\\
a_1b_2-a_2b_1
\end{pmatrix}
}.
\]
\(\mathbf a\times\mathbf b\) 同时垂直于 \(\mathbf a\) 和 \(\mathbf b\)，方向由 right-hand rule 决定，且
\[
|\mathbf a\times\mathbf b|=|\mathbf a|\,|\mathbf b|\sin\theta.
\]
因此平行四边形面积为 \(|\mathbf a\times\mathbf b|\)，三角形面积为其一半。向量积满足
\[
\mathbf a\times\mathbf b=-(\mathbf b\times\mathbf a).
\]


1.7 Distances involving lines
点 \(P\) 到直线 \(\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf d\) 的距离可写成
\[
\boxed{
D=\frac{|(\mathbf p-\mathbf a)\times\mathbf d|}{|\mathbf d|}
}.
\]
两条 skew lines
\[
\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf b,\;
\mathbf r=\mathbf c+\mu\mathbf d
\]
的共同垂直方向为 \(\mathbf b\times\mathbf d\)。最短距离为
\[
\boxed{
D=\frac{|(\mathbf c-\mathbf a)\boldsymbol\cdot(\mathbf b\times\mathbf d)|}
{|\mathbf b\times\mathbf d|}
}.
\]
若要求 common perpendicular 的方程，可分别取两线上一般点 \(P,Q\)，令 \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\) 同时垂直于 \(\mathbf b\) 和 \(\mathbf d\)，解出两个参数后用 \(P\) 或 \(Q\) 与方向 \(\mathbf b\times\mathbf d\) 写直线。

title: 1.6 Vectors
text:
2. Textbook Examples
本节保留教材 Chapter 7 的全部编号 Example。题意与符号按教材重写，步骤展开到可直接复习的方法层级。

Find the equation of the plane through \(A(4,2,0)\), \(B(3,1,1)\) and \(C(4,-1,1)\).






提示Solution





Two independent directions in the plane are
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\-1\\1\end{pmatrix},\;
\overrightarrow{AC}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\-3\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Hence a parametric equation is
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}4\\2\\0\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}-1\\-1\\1\end{pmatrix}
+\mu\begin{pmatrix}0\\-3\\1\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Thus \(x=4-\lambda\), \(y=2-\lambda-3\mu\) and \(z=\lambda+\mu\). Eliminating \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\) gives
\[
\boxed{2x+y+3z=10}.
\]





Write down the equation of the plane through \((2,1,3)\) whose normal is \(4\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+6\mathbf k\).






提示Solution





With \(\mathbf a=(2,1,3)\) and \(\mathbf n=(4,5,6)\),
\[
(\mathbf r-\mathbf a)\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=0.
\]
Therefore \(4(x-2)+5(y-1)+6(z-3)=0\), so
\[
\boxed{4x+5y+6z=31}.
\]





Find the point where
\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\\4\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\-1\end{pmatrix}
\]
meets the plane \(5x+y-z=1\).






提示Solution





A point of the line has coordinates \((2+\lambda,3+2\lambda,4-\lambda)\). Substitution gives
\[
5(2+\lambda)+(3+2\lambda)-(4-\lambda)=1,
\]
so \(9+8\lambda=1\) and \(\lambda=-1\). The point of intersection is
\[
\boxed{(1,1,5)}.
\]





Show that the line
\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}3\\1\\-2\end{pmatrix}
\]
is parallel to the plane \(2x+4y+5z=8\).






提示Solution





The direction of the line is \(\mathbf d=(3,1,-2)\) and a normal to the plane is \(\mathbf n=(2,4,5)\). Since
\[
\mathbf d\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=3(2)+1(4)-2(5)=0,
\]
the line direction is perpendicular to the normal. Hence the line is parallel to the plane.





Determine whether the line in Example 7.4 lies in the plane \(2x+4y+5z=8\).






提示Solution





Example 7.4 shows that the line is parallel to the plane. For \(t=1\), the point on the line is \((5,2,-2)\), and
\[
2(5)+4(2)+5(-2)=8.
\]
This point belongs to the plane. Therefore the whole line lies in the plane.





\(A\) is \((7,5,3)\) and \(\pi\) is \(3x+2y+z=6\).

Find the line through \(A\) perpendicular to \(\pi\).
Find its intersection \(P\) with \(\pi\).
Find \(AP\).







提示Solution






A normal to \(\pi\) is \((3,2,1)\), so

\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}7\\5\\3\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}3\\2\\1\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

Substitution of \((7+3\lambda,5+2\lambda,3+\lambda)\) into the plane gives

\[
3(7+3\lambda)+2(5+2\lambda)+(3+\lambda)=6.
\]
Thus \(14\lambda=-28\), so \(\lambda=-2\) and
\[
\boxed{P=(1,1,1)}.
\]



\[
\overrightarrow{AP}=\begin{pmatrix}-6\\-4\\-2\end{pmatrix},
\;
AP=\sqrt{36+16+4}=\boxed{\sqrt{56}}.
\]





Find the angle between
\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\2\\-3\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}-1\\2\\5\end{pmatrix}
\]
and the plane \(2x+3y+z=4\).






提示Solution





Take \(\mathbf n=(2,3,1)\) and \(\mathbf d=(-1,2,5)\). If \(A\) is the angle between \(\mathbf n\) and \(\mathbf d\), then
\[
\cos A=\frac{\mathbf n\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf d}{|\mathbf n||\mathbf d|}
=\frac{-2+6+5}{\sqrt{14}\sqrt{30}}.
\]
Hence \(A=63.95^\circ\). The angle between the line and the plane is
\[
90^\circ-A=26.05^\circ,
\]
or \(\boxed{26^\circ}\) to the nearest degree.





Find the line of intersection of
\[
3x+2y-3z=-18
\;\text{and}\;
x-2y+z=12.
\]






提示Solution





Putting \(y=0\) gives \(x=3\), \(z=9\), so \(P=(3,0,9)\). Putting \(z=1\) gives \(x=-1\), \(y=-6\), so \(Q=(-1,-6,1)\). Then
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}=\begin{pmatrix}-4\\-6\\-8\end{pmatrix}
=-2\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\\4\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore one equation of the common line is
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\-6\\1\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\\4\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Equivalent base points and non-zero scalar multiples of the direction vector give the same line.





Find the acute angle between \(\pi_1:2x+3y+5z=8\) and \(\pi_2:5x+y-4z=12\).






提示Solution





The normals are \(\mathbf n_1=(2,3,5)\) and \(\mathbf n_2=(5,1,-4)\). Hence
\[
\cos\theta=\frac{\mathbf n_1\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n_2}{|\mathbf n_1||\mathbf n_2|}
=\frac{-7}{\sqrt{38}\sqrt{42}}.
\]
This gives \(\theta=100.1^\circ\) between the chosen normals. The acute angle between the planes is therefore
\[
\boxed{180^\circ-100.1^\circ=79.9^\circ}.
\]





Find the plane through \((1,2,3)\) that contains the common line of
\[
\pi_1:2x+2y+z+3=0,
\;
\pi_2:2x+3y+z+13=0.
\]






提示Solution





Every plane in the sheaf through the common line has equation
\[
p(2x+2y+z+3)+q(2x+3y+z+13)=0,
\]
where \(p\) and \(q\) are not both zero. Substitution of \((1,2,3)\) gives
\[
12p+24q=0,
\]
so \(p=-2q\). Therefore
\[
-2(2x+2y+z+3)+(2x+3y+z+13)=0,
\]
and the required plane is
\[
\boxed{2x+y+z=7}.
\]





Find the equation of the common perpendicular to
\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\-1\end{pmatrix}
+\alpha\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\0\end{pmatrix},
\;
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\1\\4\end{pmatrix}
+\beta\begin{pmatrix}-3\\0\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]






提示Solution





Let
\[
P=(1+\alpha,\alpha,-1),
\;
Q=(-2-3\beta,1,4+\beta).
\]
Then
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}=(-3-\alpha-3\beta,1-\alpha,5+\beta).
\]
For \(PQ\) to be perpendicular to both given lines,
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(1,1,0)=0,
\;
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(-3,0,1)=0.
\]
Thus
\[
-2\alpha-3\beta-2=0,
\;
3\alpha+10\beta+14=0.
\]
Solving gives \(\alpha=2\), \(\beta=-2\). Hence \(P=(3,2,-1)\), \(Q=(4,1,2)\) and \(\overrightarrow{PQ}=(1,-1,3)\). The common perpendicular is
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}3\\2\\-1\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\3\end{pmatrix}}.
\]





Let \(\mathbf a=3\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+5\mathbf k\) and \(\mathbf b=\mathbf i-4\mathbf j+2\mathbf k\).

Calculate \(\mathbf a\times\mathbf b\).
Hence find a unit vector perpendicular to both \(\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf b\).







提示Solution








\[
\mathbf a\times\mathbf b=
\begin{vmatrix}
\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\
3&2&5\\
1&-4&2
\end{vmatrix}
=24\mathbf i-\mathbf j-14\mathbf k.
\]

Since \(|\mathbf a\times\mathbf b|=\sqrt{24^2+(-1)^2+(-14)^2}=\sqrt{773}\), one required unit vector is

\[
\boxed{\widehat{\mathbf n}=\frac1{\sqrt{773}}
\begin{pmatrix}24\\-1\\-14\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Its negative is also perpendicular to both vectors.





Find the Cartesian equation of the plane through \(A(3,4,2)\), \(B(2,0,5)\) and \(C(6,7,8)\).






提示Solution





\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(-1,-4,3),
\;
\overrightarrow{BC}=(4,7,3).
\]
A normal is
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{BC}
=(-33,15,9)=-3(11,-5,-3).
\]
Use \(\mathbf n=(11,-5,-3)\). The equation is \(11x-5y-3z=d\). Substitution of \(A\) gives \(d=33-20-6=7\). Hence
\[
\boxed{11x-5y-3z=7}.
\]





A plane is
\[
\mathbf r=3\mathbf i-\mathbf j+5\mathbf k
+\lambda(5\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k)
+\mu(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j-3\mathbf k).
\]
Find its Cartesian equation.






提示Solution





A normal is the vector product of the two directions:
\[
\begin{pmatrix}5\\-2\\1\end{pmatrix}
\times
\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\\-3\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}5\\17\\9\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\mathbf r\boldsymbol\cdot(5,17,9)
=(3,-1,5)\boldsymbol\cdot(5,17,9)=43,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{5x+17y+9z=43}.
\]





The line \(l\) is
\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}-10\\20\\2\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}5\\4\\3\end{pmatrix}
\]
and \(P=(70,30,22)\). The point \(M\) on \(l\) is closest to \(P\).

Express \(\mathbf m\) and \(\overrightarrow{PM}\) in terms of \(\lambda\).
Show that \(\lambda=10\) and find \(M\).
Verify the value of \(PM\).







提示Solution








\[
\mathbf m=\begin{pmatrix}-10+5\lambda\\20+4\lambda\\2+3\lambda\end{pmatrix},
\;
\overrightarrow{PM}=\begin{pmatrix}-80+5\lambda\\-10+4\lambda\\-20+3\lambda\end{pmatrix}.
\]

At the nearest point, \(PM\) is perpendicular to the line direction \(\mathbf d=(5,4,3)\):

\[
5(-80+5\lambda)+4(-10+4\lambda)+3(-20+3\lambda)=0.
\]
Thus \(50\lambda=500\), so \(\lambda=10\) and
\[
\boxed{M=(40,60,32)}.
\]

\(\overrightarrow{PM}=(-30,30,10)\), hence

\[
PM=\sqrt{900+900+100}=\boxed{10\sqrt{19}}.
\]





Find the shortest distance from \(P(3,5)\) to \(5x-3y+4=0\).






提示Solution





Using the two-dimensional distance formula,
\[
D=\frac{|5(3)-3(5)+4|}{\sqrt{5^2+(-3)^2}}
=\boxed{\frac4{\sqrt{34}}}.
\]
This example is retained because it is a numbered textbook example; the main Further Mathematics vector work uses the corresponding three-dimensional methods.





Find the shortest distance from \((2,4,-2)\) to \(6x-y-3z+1=0\).






提示Solution





\[
D=\frac{|6(2)-4-3(-2)+1|}{\sqrt{6^2+(-1)^2+(-3)^2}}
=\frac{15}{\sqrt{46}}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{D=\frac{15}{\sqrt{46}}\approx2.21}.
\]





The lines are
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\\0\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\-3\\2\end{pmatrix},
\;
l_2:\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}4\\2\\1\end{pmatrix}
+\mu\begin{pmatrix}-2\\6\\-4\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Show that they are parallel.
Find the shortest distance between them.







提示Solution






The second direction is \(-2\) times the first, so the lines are parallel.
Take \(A=(2,-3,0)\) on \(l_1\) and \(P=(4,2,1)\) on \(l_2\). Then

\[
\overrightarrow{AP}=(2,5,1),
\;
\overrightarrow{AP}\times(1,-3,2)=(13,-3,-11).
\]
Therefore
\[
D=\frac{\sqrt{13^2+(-3)^2+(-11)^2}}{\sqrt{1^2+(-3)^2+2^2}}
=\boxed{\sqrt{\frac{299}{14}}\approx4.62}.
\]





Find the shortest distance between
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}8\\9\\-2\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\-3\end{pmatrix},
\;
l_2:\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}6\\0\\-2\end{pmatrix}
+\mu\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\-2\end{pmatrix}.
\]






提示Solution





Let \(\mathbf a_1=(8,9,-2)\), \(\mathbf a_2=(6,0,-2)\), \(\mathbf d_1=(1,2,-3)\) and \(\mathbf d_2=(1,-1,-2)\). Then
\[
\mathbf a_1-\mathbf a_2=(2,9,0),
\;
\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2=(-7,-1,-3).
\]
Also
\[
(\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2)\boldsymbol\cdot(\mathbf a_1-\mathbf a_2)=-23,
\;
|\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2|=\sqrt{59}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{D=\frac{23}{\sqrt{59}}\approx2.99}.
\]

title: 1.6 Vectors
section: 3. Cambridge examination questions in the textbook
text:
3. Cambridge examination questions in the textbook
这里只收录教材 Exercise 中明确标注 Cambridge International AS & A Level Further Mathematics 9231 来源的题目；标注为 Mathematics 9709 的题目不在本节重复收录。






注记Exercise 7B, Question 13



The lines \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) have equations
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=8\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+3\mathbf k
+\lambda(\mathbf i-2\mathbf j)
\]
and
\[
l_2:\mathbf r=5\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-14\mathbf k
+\mu(-2\mathbf j+3\mathbf k).
\]
The point \(P\) on \(l_1\) and the point \(Q\) on \(l_2\) are such that \(PQ\) is perpendicular to both lines. Find the position vectors of \(P\) and \(Q\).
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Question 11 (part question), May/June 2015. The sign of the \(\mathbf k\) term is given here in the form consistent with the original mark scheme and the textbook answer.






提示Answer





Write
\[
P=(8+\lambda,2-2\lambda,3),
\;
Q=(5,3-2\mu,-14+3\mu).
\]
Then
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}=(-3-\lambda,1-2\mu+2\lambda,-17+3\mu).
\]
The two perpendicularity conditions give
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(1,-2,0)=0
\Longrightarrow -5-5\lambda+4\mu=0,
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(0,-2,3)=0
\Longrightarrow -53-4\lambda+13\mu=0.
\]
Solving gives \(\lambda=3\) and \(\mu=5\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\overrightarrow{OP}=11\mathbf i-4\mathbf j+3\mathbf k},
\;
\boxed{\overrightarrow{OQ}=5\mathbf i-7\mathbf j+\mathbf k}.
\]











注记Exercise 7C, Question 10



The plane \(\Pi_1\) has equation
\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\\-1\end{pmatrix}
+s\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\1\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\-2\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Find a Cartesian equation of \(\Pi_1\).

The plane \(\Pi_2\) has equation \(2x-y+z=10\).

Find the acute angle between \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_2\).
Find an equation of their line of intersection in the form \(\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf b\).

Source: 9231 Paper 11 Question 8, October/November 2013.






提示Answer






A normal to \(\Pi_1\) is

\[
\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\1\end{pmatrix}
\times
\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\-2\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1\\3\\-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Hence
\[
x+3y-z=(2)+3(3)-(-1)=12,
\]
so \(\boxed{\Pi_1:x+3y-z=12}\).

Use normals \(\mathbf n_1=(1,3,-1)\) and \(\mathbf n_2=(2,-1,1)\):

\[
\cos\theta= rac{|\mathbf n_1\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n_2|}{|\mathbf n_1||\mathbf n_2|}
=\frac{|2-3-1|}{\sqrt{11}\sqrt6}
=\frac2{\sqrt{66}}.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{\theta=75.7^\circ}\).

A direction of the common line is

\[
\mathbf n_1\times\mathbf n_2
=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\\-7\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The point \((6,2,0)\) satisfies both plane equations. Therefore
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}6\\2\\0\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\\-7\end{pmatrix}}.
\]











注记Exercise 7D, Question 11



The line \(l_1\) passes through \(A(2,3,-5)\) and \(B(8,7,-13)\). The line \(l_2\) passes through \(C(-2,1,8)\) and \(D(3,-1,4)\).

Find the shortest distance between \(l_1\) and \(l_2\).
The plane \(\Pi_1\) passes through \(A,B,D\), and \(\Pi_2\) passes through \(A,C,D\). Find the acute angle between \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_2\).

Source: 9231 Paper 11 Question 11, May/June 2014.






提示Answer






Direction vectors are

\[
\mathbf d_1=\overrightarrow{AB}=(6,4,-8),
\;
\mathbf d_2=\overrightarrow{CD}=(5,-2,-4).
\]
Also
\[
\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2=(-32,-16,-32),
\;
\overrightarrow{AC}=(-4,-2,13).
\]
Therefore
\[
D=\frac{|\overrightarrow{AC}\boldsymbol\cdot(\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2)|}
{|\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2|}
=\frac{256}{48}
=\boxed{\frac{16}{3}}.
\]

Suitable normals are

\[
\mathbf n_1=\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AD}
=(4,-62,-28)=2(2,-31,-14),
\]
\[
\mathbf n_2=\overrightarrow{AC}\times\overrightarrow{AD}
=(34,49,18).
\]
Thus
\[
\cos\theta= rac{|(2,-31,-14)\boldsymbol\cdot(34,49,18)|}
{\sqrt{1161}\sqrt{3881}}
=\frac{1703}{\sqrt{1161\cdot3881}}.
\]
Hence the acute angle is \(\boxed{36.7^\circ}\).











注记Exercise 7D, Question 12



The position vectors of \(A,B,C,D\) are
\[
2\mathbf i+4\mathbf j-3\mathbf k,
\;
-2\mathbf i+5\mathbf j-4\mathbf k,
\;
\mathbf i+4\mathbf j+\mathbf k,
\;
\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+m\mathbf k,
\]
respectively, where \(m\) is an integer. The shortest distance between \(AB\) and \(CD\) is \(3\).

Show that the only possible value of \(m\) is \(2\).
Find the shortest distance of \(D\) from \(AC\).
Show that the acute angle between planes \(ACD\) and \(BCD\) is \(\cos^{-1}(1/3)\).

Source: 9231 Paper 11 Question 11, May/June 2012.






提示Answer








\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(-4,1,-1),
\;
\overrightarrow{CD}=(0,1,m-1),
\;
\overrightarrow{AC}=(-1,0,4).
\]
Now
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{CD}
=(m,4m-4,-4).
\]
Using the skew-line distance formula,
\[
\frac{|\overrightarrow{AC}\boldsymbol\cdot
(\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{CD})|}
{|\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{CD}|}=3.
\]
After squaring,
\[
(m+16)^2=9\{m^2+16(m-1)^2+16\},
\]
which reduces to
\[
19m^2-40m+4=0.
\]
Hence \(m=2\) or \(m=2/19\). Since \(m\) is an integer,
\[
\boxed{m=2}.
\]

With \(m=2\), \(D=(1,5,2)\) and

\[
\overrightarrow{AD}=(-1,1,5),
\;
\overrightarrow{AC}=(-1,0,4).
\]
Therefore
\[
D_{D,AC}=\frac{|\overrightarrow{AD}\times\overrightarrow{AC}|}{|\overrightarrow{AC}|}
=\frac{\sqrt{18}}{\sqrt{17}}
=\boxed{\sqrt{\frac{18}{17}}}.
\]

Normals to \(ACD\) and \(BCD\) may be taken as

\[
\mathbf n_1=\overrightarrow{AC}\times\overrightarrow{AD}=(-4,1,-1),
\]
\[
\mathbf n_2=\overrightarrow{BC}\times\overrightarrow{BD}=(-6,-3,3).
\]
Then
\[
\frac{|\mathbf n_1\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n_2|}{|\mathbf n_1||\mathbf n_2|}
=\frac{18}{\sqrt{18}\sqrt{54}}=\frac13.
\]
Thus the acute angle is
\[
\boxed{\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac13\right)}.
\]

title: 1.6 Vectors
text:
4. Past-paper question bank
完全相同的地区版本合并为一题，并在题目下列出全部来源。答案按 published mark scheme 的得分点展开。

2019






注记May/June 2019, Paper 11/12, Question 3



The lines are
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=6\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+7\mathbf k+\lambda(\mathbf i+\mathbf j),
\]
\[
l_2:\mathbf r=4\mathbf i+4\mathbf j+\mu(-6\mathbf j+\mathbf k).
\]
Points \(P\) on \(l_1\) and \(Q\) on \(l_2\) are such that \(PQ\) is perpendicular to both lines. Find their position vectors. [8]
Sources: 9231/11/M/J/19 Q3; 9231/12/M/J/19 Q3.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





\[
P=(6+\lambda,2+\lambda,7),
\;Q=(4,4-6\mu,\mu),
\]
so
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}=(-2-\lambda,2-\lambda-6\mu,-7+\mu).
\]
The perpendicularity conditions give
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(1,1,0)=0
\Longrightarrow -2\lambda-6\mu=0,
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(0,-6,1)=0
\Longrightarrow 6\lambda+37\mu=19.
\]
Thus \(\lambda=-3\), \(\mu=1\), and
\[
\boxed{\overrightarrow{OP}=3\mathbf i-\mathbf j+7\mathbf k},
\;\boxed{\overrightarrow{OQ}=4\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k}.
\]











注记May/June 2019, Paper 13, Question 7



Line \(l_1\) passes through \(A(-3,1,4)\) and \(B(-1,5,9)\). Line \(l_2\) passes through \(C(-2,6,5)\) and \(D(-1,7,5)\).

Find the shortest distance between \(l_1\) and \(l_2\). [5]
Find the acute angle between \(l_2\) and plane \(ABD\). [5]

Source: 9231/13/M/J/19 Q7.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(2,4,5),
\;\overrightarrow{CD}=(1,1,0),
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{CD}=(-5,5,-2).
\]
Using \(\overrightarrow{AC}=(1,5,1)\),
\[
D=\frac{|(1,5,1)\boldsymbol\cdot(-5,5,-2)|}{\sqrt{54}}
=\boxed{\frac{18}{\sqrt{54}}=\sqrt6}.
\]

Since \(\overrightarrow{AD}=(2,6,1)\), a normal to \(ABD\) is

\[
(2,4,5)\times(2,6,1)=(-26,8,4)=2(-13,4,2).
\]
For the line direction \((1,1,0)\),
\[
\sin\alpha=\frac{|(1,1,0)\boldsymbol\cdot(-13,4,2)|}{\sqrt2\sqrt{189}}
=\frac9{\sqrt{378}}.
\]
Hence \(\boxed{\alpha=27.6^\circ}\).











注记October/November 2019, Paper 11/12/13, Question 6



With \(O\) as origin, \(A,B,C\) have position vectors \(\mathbf i-\mathbf j\), \(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j+7\mathbf k\) and \(\mathbf i-\mathbf j+\mathbf k\).

Find the shortest distance between lines \(OC\) and \(AB\). [5]
Find the Cartesian equation of the plane containing \(OC\) and the common perpendicular of \(OC\) and \(AB\). [4]

Sources: 9231/11/O/N/19 Q6; 9231/12/O/N/19 Q6; 9231/13/O/N/19 Q6.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






Directions are \(\overrightarrow{OC}=(1,-1,1)\) and \(\overrightarrow{AB}=(1,2,7)\). Thus

\[
\overrightarrow{OC}\times\overrightarrow{AB}=(-9,-6,3)=-3(3,2,-1).
\]
Using \(\overrightarrow{OA}=(1,-1,0)\),
\[
D=\frac{|(1,-1,0)\boldsymbol\cdot(3,2,-1)|}{\sqrt{14}}
=\boxed{\frac1{\sqrt{14}}}.
\]

The required plane contains directions \((1,-1,1)\) and \((3,2,-1)\). Its normal is

\[
(1,-1,1)\times(3,2,-1)=(-1,4,5).
\]
It passes through \(O\), so
\[
\boxed{-x+4y+5z=0}.
\]







2020






注记May/June 2020, Paper 11/12, Question 5



\(l_1:\mathbf r=(3,0,3)+m(1,4,4)\) and \(l_2:\mathbf r=(3,-5,-6)+n(0,5,6)\).

Find their shortest distance. [5]
A plane \(\Pi\) contains \(l_1\) and is parallel to \((1,0,1)\). Find its Cartesian equation. [4]

Sources: 9231/11/M/J/20 Q5; 9231/12/M/J/20 Q5.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
(1,4,4)\times(0,5,6)=(4,-6,5),
\]
\[
D=\frac{|(0,-5,-9)\boldsymbol\cdot(4,-6,5)|}{\sqrt{77}}
=\boxed{\frac{15}{\sqrt{77}}}.
\]

A normal is \((1,4,4)\times(1,0,1)=(4,3,-4)\). Hence

\[
\boxed{4x+3y-4z=0}.
\]











注记May/June 2020, Paper 13, Question 7



\(l_1:\mathbf r=-5\mathbf j+m(5\mathbf i+2\mathbf k)\) and \(l_2:\mathbf r=4\mathbf i+2\mathbf j-2\mathbf k+n(\mathbf j+\mathbf k)\). A plane \(\Pi\) contains \(l_1\) and is parallel to \(l_2\).

Find the Cartesian equation of \(\Pi\). [4]
Find the distance between \(l_2\) and \(\Pi\). [3]
Points \(P\) on \(l_1\) and \(Q\) on \(l_2\) make \(PQ\) perpendicular to both lines. Show that \(\overrightarrow{OP}=\frac{55}{27}\mathbf i-5\mathbf j+\frac{22}{27}\mathbf k\) and state an equation of \(PQ\). [8]

Source: 9231/13/M/J/20 Q7.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






A normal is \((5,0,2)\times(0,1,1)=(-2,-5,5)\). Thus

\[
\boxed{-2x-5y+5z=25}.
\]

Using \((4,2,-2)\) on \(l_2\),

\[
\boxed{D=\frac{53}{\sqrt{54}}}.
\]

Let \(P=(5m,-5,2m)\) and \(Q=(4,2+n,-2+n)\). From \(PQ\boldsymbol\cdot(5,0,2)=0\) and \(PQ\boldsymbol\cdot(0,1,1)=0\), solving gives \(m=11/27\). Hence the stated \(P\) follows. Since the common perpendicular direction is \((-2,-5,5)\),

\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}55/27\\-5\\22/27\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}-2\\-5\\5\end{pmatrix}}.
\]











注记October/November 2020, Paper 11/13, Question 4



\(A,B,C\) have position vectors \((-1,1,2)\), \((-2,-1,0)\) and \((2,0,2)\).

Find plane \(ABC\). [5] (b) Find its distance from \(O\). [2] (c) Find the acute angle between planes \(OAB\) and \(ABC\). [4]

Sources: 9231/11/O/N/20 Q4; 9231/13/O/N/20 Q4.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






\(\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=(-2,-6,7)\), so

\[
\boxed{-2x-6y+7z=10}.
\]

\(\boxed{10/\sqrt{89}}\).
A normal to \(OAB\) is \((2,-4,3)\). Thus

\[
\cos\theta=\frac{41}{\sqrt{29}\sqrt{89}},
\]
so \(\boxed{\theta=36.2^\circ}\).











注记October/November 2020, Paper 12, Question 7



\(A,B,C\) have position vectors \((-2,2,-1)\), \((-2,1,2)\) and \((0,-2,1)\).

Find plane \(ABC\). [5] (b) Find the acute angle between planes \(OBC\) and \(ABC\). [4]

The point \(D\) has position vector \(t\mathbf i-\mathbf j\). (c) Given that the shortest distance between \(AB\) and \(CD\) is \(\sqrt{10}\), find \(t\). [6]
Source: 9231/12/O/N/20 Q7.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






\(\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=2(5,3,1)\), hence

\[
\boxed{5x+3y+z=-5}.
\]

A normal to \(OBC\) is \((5,2,4)\). Therefore

\[
\cos\theta=\frac{35}{\sqrt{35}\sqrt{45}},
\]
giving \(\boxed{\theta=28.1^\circ}\).

\(\overrightarrow{AB}=(0,-1,3)\), \(\overrightarrow{CD}=(t,1,-1)\) and their vector product is \((-2,3t,t)\). Thus

\[
\frac{|(2,-4,2)\boldsymbol\cdot(-2,3t,t)|}{\sqrt{4+10t^2}}=\sqrt{10}.
\]
Squaring reduces to \(80t=24\), so \(\boxed{t=3/10}\).







2021






注记May/June 2021, Paper 11/12, Question 6



Let \(t>0\). The line \(l_1\) passes through \(t\mathbf i+\mathbf j\) and is parallel to \(-2\mathbf i-\mathbf j\). The line \(l_2\) passes through \(\mathbf j+t\mathbf k\) and is parallel to \(-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k\). The shortest distance between the lines is \(\sqrt{21}\).

Find \(t\). [5]
The plane \(\Pi_1\) contains \(l_1\) and is parallel to \(l_2\). Write a parametric equation of \(\Pi_1\). [1]
The plane \(\Pi_2\) is \(5x-6y+7z=0\). Find the acute angle between \(l_2\) and \(\Pi_2\). [3]
Find the acute angle between \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_2\). [3]

Sources: 9231/11/M/J/21 Q6; 9231/12/M/J/21 Q6.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






A vector joining the base points is \(t(-1,0,1)\), while

\[
(-2,-1,0)\times(0,-2,1)=(-1,2,4).
\]
Hence
\[
\frac{|t(-1,0,1)\boldsymbol\cdot(-1,2,4)|}{\sqrt{21}}
=\frac{5t}{\sqrt{21}}=\sqrt{21},
\]
so \(\boxed{t=\dfrac{21}{5}}\).



\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\frac{21}{5}\mathbf i+\mathbf j
+\lambda(-2\mathbf i-\mathbf j)
+\mu(-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k)}.
\]

If \(\alpha\) is the angle between \(l_2\) and \(\Pi_2\), then

\[
\sin\alpha=\frac{|(0,-2,1)\boldsymbol\cdot(5,-6,7)|}{\sqrt5\sqrt{110}}
=\frac{19}{\sqrt{550}}.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{\alpha=54.1^\circ}\).

A normal to \(\Pi_1\) is \((-1,2,4)\). Therefore

\[
\cos\theta=\frac{|(-1,2,4)\boldsymbol\cdot(5,-6,7)|}{\sqrt{21}\sqrt{110}}
=\frac{11}{\sqrt{2310}},
\]
giving \(\boxed{\theta=76.8^\circ}\).











注记May/June 2021, Paper 13, Question 6



The lines are
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=-\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k+s(2\mathbf i-3\mathbf j),
\]
\[
l_2:\mathbf r=3\mathbf i-2\mathbf k+t(3\mathbf i-\mathbf j+3\mathbf k).
\]
Plane \(\Pi_1\) contains \(l_1\) and \(P(-2,-2,4)\). Plane \(\Pi_2\) contains \(l_2\) and is parallel to \(l_1\).

Give a parametric equation of \(\Pi_1\). [2]
Find a Cartesian equation of \(\Pi_2\). [4]
Find the acute angle between the planes. [5]

Source: 9231/13/M/J/21 Q6.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






From \(P\) to \((-1,-2,1)\) on \(l_1\) is \((1,0,-3)\), hence

\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\-2\\4\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\\0\end{pmatrix}
+\mu\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\-3\end{pmatrix}}.
\]



\[
(2,-3,0)\times(3,-1,3)=(-9,-6,7).
\]
Using \((3,0,-2)\) gives
\[
\boxed{9x+6y-7z=41}.
\]

A normal to \(\Pi_1\) is \((3,2,1)\). Thus

\[
\cos\theta=\frac{|(3,2,1)\boldsymbol\cdot(9,6,-7)|}{\sqrt{14}\sqrt{166}}
=\frac{32}{\sqrt{2324}},
\]
so \(\boxed{\theta=48.4^\circ}\).











注记October/November 2021, Paper 11/13, Question 5



The plane \(\Pi\) is
\[
\mathbf r=-2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+3\mathbf k
+m(\mathbf i+\mathbf k)+n(2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j).
\]

Find its Cartesian equation. [4]

The line \(l\) passes through \(P(2,-3,5)\) and is parallel to \(\mathbf k\).

Find where \(l\) meets \(\Pi\). [3]
Find the acute angle between \(l\) and \(\Pi\). [3]
Find the perpendicular distance from \(P\) to \(\Pi\). [3]

Sources: 9231/11/O/N/21 Q5; 9231/13/O/N/21 Q5.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
(1,0,1)\times(2,3,0)=(-3,2,3),
\]
and substitution of \((-2,3,3)\) gives
\[
\boxed{-3x+2y+3z=21}.
\]

A general point of \(l\) is \((2,-3,5+t)\). Substitution gives \(t=6\), so the intersection is

\[
\boxed{(2,-3,11)}.
\]



\[
\sin\alpha=\frac{|(0,0,1)\boldsymbol\cdot(-3,2,3)|}{\sqrt{22}}
=\frac3{\sqrt{22}},
\]
so \(\boxed{\alpha=39.8^\circ}\).



\[
D=\frac{|-3(2)+2(-3)+3(5)-21|}{\sqrt{22}}
=\boxed{\frac{18}{\sqrt{22}}\approx3.84}.
\]











注记October/November 2021, Paper 12, Question 7



The points \(A,B,C\) have position vectors \(2\mathbf i+2\mathbf j\), \(-\mathbf j+\mathbf k\) and \(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j-7\mathbf k\).

Find the equation of plane \(OAB\) in the form \(\mathbf r\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=p\). [3]

The plane \(\Pi\) is \(x-3y-2z=1\).

Find its perpendicular distance from \(O\). [1]
Find the acute angle between \(OAB\) and \(\Pi\). [3]
Find an equation of the common perpendicular to lines \(OC\) and \(AB\). [10]

Source: 9231/12/O/N/21 Q7.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
(2,2,0)\times(0,-1,1)=(2,-2,-2),
\]
so \(\boxed{\mathbf r\boldsymbol\cdot(1,-1,-1)=0}\).

\(\boxed{1/\sqrt{14}}\).


\[
\cos\theta=\frac{|(1,-1,-1)\boldsymbol\cdot(1,-3,-2)|}{\sqrt3\sqrt{14}}
=\frac6{\sqrt{42}},
\]
so \(\boxed{\theta=22.2^\circ}\).

Directions of \(OC\) and \(AB\) are \((2,1,-7)\) and \((-2,-3,1)\). Their vector product is parallel to \((5,-3,1)\). Let \(P=\lambda(2,1,-7)\) and \(Q=(2,2,0)+\mu(-2,-3,1)\). Solving

\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(2,1,-7)=0,
\;
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(-2,-3,1)=0
\]
gives a point \((-1/5,-1/10,7/10)\) on the common perpendicular. Hence
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}-1/5\\-1/10\\7/10\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}5\\-3\\1\end{pmatrix}}.
\]







2022






注记May/June 2022, Paper 11/12, Question 2



The points \(A,B,C\) have position vectors
\[
4\mathbf i-4\mathbf j+\mathbf k,
\;-4\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-4\mathbf k,
\;4\mathbf i-\mathbf j-2\mathbf k.
\]

Find the equation of plane \(ABC\). [5]
Find the perpendicular distance from \(O\) to plane \(ABC\). [2]

The point \(D\) has position vector \(2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-3\mathbf k\).

Find the intersection of line \(OD\) with plane \(ABC\). [3]

Sources: 9231/11/M/J/22 Q2; 9231/12/M/J/22 Q2.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(-8,7,-5),
\;\overrightarrow{AC}=(0,3,-3),
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=(-6,-24,-24),
\]
so take the normal \((1,4,4)\). Substitution of \(A\) gives
\[
\boxed{x+4y+4z=-8}.
\]



\[
\boxed{D=\frac8{\sqrt{33}}\approx1.39}.
\]

Line \(OD\) is

\[
\mathbf r=t\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\\-3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Substitution gives \(2t+12t-12t=-8\), so \(t=-4\). The intersection is
\[
\boxed{(-8,-12,12)}.
\]











注记May/June 2022, Paper 13, Question 7



The position vectors of \(A,B,C,D\) are
\[
7\mathbf i+4\mathbf j-\mathbf k,
\;11\mathbf i+3\mathbf j,
\;2\mathbf i+6\mathbf j+3\mathbf k,
\;2\mathbf i+7\mathbf j+m\mathbf k.
\]

Given that the shortest distance between lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) is \(3\), show that \(m^2-5m+4=0\). [7]

Let \(\Pi_1\) be plane \(ABD\) when \(m=1\), and \(\Pi_2\) be plane \(ABD\) when \(m=4\).
(b)(i) Write a parametric equation of \(\Pi_1\). [2]
(b)(ii) Find a Cartesian equation of \(\Pi_2\). [4]

Find the acute angle between \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_2\). [5]

Source: 9231/13/M/J/22 Q7.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(4,-1,1),
\;\overrightarrow{CD}=(0,1,m-3),
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{CD}
=(2-m,12-4m,4).
\]
Using \(\overrightarrow{AC}=(-5,2,4)\), the distance condition is
\[
\frac{|(-5,2,4)\boldsymbol\cdot(2-m,12-4m,4)|}
{\sqrt{(m-2)^2+(4m-12)^2+16}}=3.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{|30-3m|}{\sqrt{17m^2-100m+164}}=3.
\]
Squaring and simplifying gives
\[
16m^2-80m+64=0,
\]
and hence
\[
\boxed{m^2-5m+4=0}.
\]
(b)(i) When \(m=1\), \(\overrightarrow{AD}=(-5,3,2)\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}7\\4\\-1\end{pmatrix}
+s\begin{pmatrix}4\\-1\\1\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}-5\\3\\2\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(b)(ii) When \(m=4\), \(\overrightarrow{AD}=(-5,3,5)\) and
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AD}=(-8,-25,7).
\]
Substitution of \(A\) gives
\[
\boxed{-8x-25y+7z=-163}.
\]

A normal to \(\Pi_1\) is

\[
(4,-1,1)\times(-5,3,2)=(-5,-13,7).
\]
Using \(\mathbf n_2=(-8,-25,7)\),
\[
\cos\theta=\frac{|\mathbf n_1\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n_2|}
{|\mathbf n_1||\mathbf n_2|}
=\frac{414}{\sqrt{243}\sqrt{738}}.
\]
Hence \(\boxed{\theta=12.1^\circ}\).







2023






注记October/November 2023, Paper 11/13, Question 4



The lines are
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=-2\mathbf i-3\mathbf j-5\mathbf k
+m(-4\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+5\mathbf k),
\]
\[
l_2:\mathbf r=2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+3\mathbf k
+n(2\mathbf i-3\mathbf j+\mathbf k).
\]

Find the shortest distance between \(l_1\) and \(l_2\). [5]

The plane \(\Pi\) contains \(l_1\) and the point with position vector \(-\mathbf i-3\mathbf j-4\mathbf k\).

Find a Cartesian equation of \(\Pi\). [4]

Sources: 9231/11/O/N/23 Q4; 9231/13/O/N/23 Q4.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






The vector from the base point of \(l_1\) to that of \(l_2\) is \((4,1,8)\). A common perpendicular direction is

\[
(-4,3,5)\times(2,-3,1)=(18,14,6)=2(9,7,3).
\]
Hence
\[
D=\frac{|(4,1,8)\boldsymbol\cdot(9,7,3)|}{\sqrt{139}}
=\boxed{\frac{67}{\sqrt{139}}\approx5.68}.
\]

From \((-2,-3,-5)\) to the extra point \((-1,-3,-4)\) the direction is \((1,0,1)\). Therefore a normal to \(\Pi\) is

\[
(1,0,1)\times(-4,3,5)=(-3,-9,3),
\]
which is parallel to \((1,3,-1)\). Using \((-1,-3,-4)\) gives
\[
\boxed{x+3y-z=-6}.
\]











注记October/November 2023, Paper 12, Question 5



The plane \(\Pi_1\) has equation
\[
\mathbf r=\mathbf i-\mathbf j-2\mathbf k
+m(\mathbf i-2\mathbf j-3\mathbf k)
+n(3\mathbf i-\mathbf k).
\]

Find a Cartesian equation of \(\Pi_1\). [4]

The line \(l\), which does not lie in \(\Pi_1\), is
\[
\mathbf r=-3\mathbf i+\mathbf k+t(\mathbf i+\mathbf j+\mathbf k).
\]

Show that \(l\) is parallel to \(\Pi_1\). [2]
Find the distance between \(l\) and \(\Pi_1\). [3]

The plane \(\Pi_2\) is \(3x+3y+2z=1\).

Find a vector equation of the line of intersection of \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_2\). [4]

Source: 9231/12/O/N/23 Q5.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
(1,-2,-3)\times(3,0,-1)=(2,-8,6)=2(1,-4,3).
\]
Using \((1,-1,-2)\) gives
\[
\boxed{x-4y+3z=-1}.
\]

The line direction is \((1,1,1)\) and

\[
(1,1,1)\boldsymbol\cdot(1,-4,3)=0.
\]
Thus \(l\) is parallel to \(\Pi_1\); the stated condition confirms that it is not contained in the plane.

Use the point \((-3,0,1)\) on \(l\):

\[
D=\frac{|-3-4(0)+3(1)+1|}{\sqrt{26}}
=\boxed{\frac1{\sqrt{26}}\approx0.196}.
\]

The direction of the common line is

\[
(1,-4,3)\times(3,3,2)=(-17,7,15).
\]
One common point is \((5/7,0,-4/7)\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}5/7\\0\\-4/7\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}-17\\7\\15\end{pmatrix}}.
\]







2024






注记May/June 2024, Paper 11/12, Question 5



The points \(A,B,C\) have position vectors
\[
2\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+4\mathbf k,
\;2\mathbf i+4\mathbf j-\mathbf k,
\;-3\mathbf i-3\mathbf j+4\mathbf k.
\]

Find the equation of plane \(ABC\). [5]

The point \(D\) has position vector \(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j+3\mathbf k\).

Find the perpendicular distance from \(D\) to plane \(ABC\). [2]
Find the shortest distance between lines \(AB\) and \(CD\). [5]

Sources: 9231/11/M/J/24 Q5; 9231/12/M/J/24 Q5.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(0,2,-5),
\;\overrightarrow{AC}=(-5,-5,0),
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=(-25,25,10)=5(-5,5,2).
\]
Using \(A=(2,2,4)\) gives \(d=8\), hence
\[
\boxed{-5x+5y+2z=8}.
\]



\[
D=\frac{|-5(2)+5(1)+2(3)-8|}{\sqrt{54}}
=\boxed{\frac7{\sqrt{54}}\approx0.953}.
\]

\(\overrightarrow{CD}=(5,4,-1)\) and

\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{CD}=(18,-25,-10).
\]
Using \(\overrightarrow{CA}=(5,5,0)\),
\[
D=\frac{|(5,5,0)\boldsymbol\cdot(18,-25,-10)|}{\sqrt{1049}}
=\boxed{\frac{35}{\sqrt{1049}}\approx1.08}.
\]











注记May/June 2024, Paper 13, Question 5



The lines are
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=\mathbf i+4\mathbf j-\mathbf k+m(\mathbf j-2\mathbf k),
\]
\[
l_2:\mathbf r=-3\mathbf i+4\mathbf j+n(\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+\mathbf k).
\]

Find the shortest distance between \(l_1\) and \(l_2\). [5]

The plane \(\Pi_1\) contains \(l_1\) and is parallel to \(l_2\).

Obtain a Cartesian equation of \(\Pi_1\). [2]

The point \((1,1,1)\) lies on plane \(\Pi_2\). The line of intersection of \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_2\) passes through \((0,0,2)\) and is parallel to \(\mathbf i+4\mathbf j-3\mathbf k\).

Obtain a Cartesian equation of \(\Pi_2\). [3]

Source: 9231/13/M/J/24 Q5.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






The directions are \(\mathbf d_1=(0,1,-2)\) and \(\mathbf d_2=(1,2,1)\), so

\[
\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2=(5,-2,-1).
\]
For points \((1,4,-1)\) and \((-3,4,0)\), the joining vector is \((-4,0,1)\). Thus
\[
D=\frac{|(-4,0,1)\boldsymbol\cdot(5,-2,-1)|}{\sqrt{30}}
=\boxed{\frac{21}{\sqrt{30}}\approx3.83}.
\]

The vector \((5,-2,-1)\) is normal to \(\Pi_1\). Substitution of \((1,4,-1)\) gives

\[
\boxed{5x-2y-z=-2}.
\]

The plane contains the directions \((1,4,-3)\) and \((1,1,-1)\), the latter joining \((0,0,2)\) to \((1,1,1)\). A normal is

\[
(1,1,-1)\times(1,4,-3)=(1,2,3).
\]
Using \((0,0,2)\) gives
\[
\boxed{x+2y+3z=6}.
\]











注记October/November 2024, Paper 11/13, Question 7



The lines are
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-2\mathbf k+m(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j+\mathbf k),
\]
\[
l_2:\mathbf r=\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+9\mathbf k+n(\mathbf i-4\mathbf j+2\mathbf k).
\]
The plane \(\Pi_1\) contains \(l_1\) and is parallel to \(l_2\).

Find the Cartesian equation of \(\Pi_1\). [4]

The plane \(\Pi_2\) contains \(l_2\) and \((2,-1,7)\).

Find the acute angle between \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_2\). [4]

Points \(P\) on \(l_1\) and \(Q\) on \(l_2\) are such that \(PQ\) is perpendicular to both lines.

Find a vector equation for \(PQ\). [7]

Sources: 9231/11/O/N/24 Q7; 9231/13/O/N/24 Q7.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
(2,1,1)\times(1,-4,2)=(6,-3,-9)=3(2,-1,-3).
\]
Using \((1,3,-2)\) gives \(2-3+6=5\), hence
\[
\boxed{2x-y-3z=5}.
\]

The directions in \(\Pi_2\) may be taken as \((1,-4,2)\) and \((1,1,-2)\), giving normal \((6,4,5)\). Therefore

\[
\cos\theta=\frac{|(2,-1,-3)\boldsymbol\cdot(6,4,5)|}{\sqrt{14}\sqrt{77}}
=\frac7{\sqrt{1078}}.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{\theta=77.7^\circ}\).

Let

\[
P=(1+2\lambda,3+\lambda,-2+\lambda),
\]
\[
Q=(1+\mu,-2-4\mu,9+2\mu).
\]
Then
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}=(\mu-2\lambda,-5-4\mu-\lambda,11+2\mu-\lambda).
\]
The conditions \(PQ\boldsymbol\cdot(2,1,1)=0\) and \(PQ\boldsymbol\cdot(1,-4,2)=0\) reduce to
\[
-6\lambda+6=0,
\;
21\mu+42=0.
\]
Hence \(\lambda=1\), \(\mu=-2\), so \(P=(3,4,-1)\) and \(Q=(-1,6,5)\). Since \(\overrightarrow{QP}=(4,-2,-6)\) is parallel to \((6,-3,-9)\), one equation is
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\6\\5\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}6\\-3\\-9\end{pmatrix}}.
\]











注记October/November 2024, Paper 12, Question 2



The line
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-\mathbf k+m(\mathbf i-\mathbf j-4\mathbf k)
\]
lies in a plane \(\Pi\) which is parallel to \(2\mathbf i+5\mathbf j-4\mathbf k\).

Find the Cartesian equation of \(\Pi\). [4]

The line \(l_2\) is parallel to \(5\mathbf i-5\mathbf j-2\mathbf k\).

Find the acute angle between \(l_2\) and \(\Pi\). [3]

Source: 9231/12/O/N/24 Q2.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






A normal is

\[
(1,-1,-4)\times(2,5,-4)=(24,-4,7).
\]
Using \((1,3,-1)\) gives
\[
\boxed{24x-4y+7z=5}.
\]

If \(\alpha\) is the angle between the line direction and the plane normal, then

\[
\cos\alpha=\frac{|(5,-5,-2)\boldsymbol\cdot(24,-4,7)|}{\sqrt{54}\sqrt{641}}
=\frac{126}{\sqrt{34614}}.
\]
The required angle is \(90^\circ-\alpha\), hence
\[
\boxed{42.6^\circ}.
\]







2025






注记May/June 2025, Paper 11/12, Question 6



The points \(A,B,C\) have position vectors
\[
\mathbf i-2\mathbf k,
\;\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+2\mathbf k,
\;2\mathbf i-\mathbf j-\mathbf k,
\]
respectively.

Find the equation of plane \(ABC\) in the form \(ax+by+cz=d\). [5]

A point \(D\) has position vector \(\mathbf i+t\mathbf k\), where \(t\ne-2\).

Find the acute angle between planes \(ABC\) and \(ABD\). [4]
Find the values of \(t\) such that the shortest distance between lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) is \(\sqrt2\). [7]

Sources: 9231/11/M/J/25 Q6; 9231/12/M/J/25 Q6.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(0,2,4),
\;
\overrightarrow{AC}=(1,-1,1).
\]
Their vector product is \((6,4,-2)=2(3,2,-1)\), so a normal is \((3,2,-1)\). Using \(A=(1,0,-2)\),
\[
3(1)+2(0)-(-2)=5.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{3x+2y-z=5}.
\]

Since \(\overrightarrow{AD}=(0,0,t+2)\) and \(t\ne-2\), the plane \(ABD\) has normal parallel to \((1,0,0)\). Therefore

\[
\cos\theta=\frac{|(3,2,-1)\boldsymbol\cdot(1,0,0)|}{\sqrt{14}}
=\frac3{\sqrt{14}},
\]
so \(\boxed{\theta=36.7^\circ}\).

Directions of \(AB\) and \(CD\) may be taken as \((0,1,2)\) and \((-1,1,t+1)\). A common perpendicular direction is

\[
(0,1,2)\times(-1,1,t+1)=(t-1,-2,1).
\]
Since \(\overrightarrow{AC}=(1,-1,1)\),
\[
D=\frac{|(1,-1,1)\boldsymbol\cdot(t-1,-2,1)|}
{\sqrt{(t-1)^2+4+1}}
=\frac{|t+2|}{\sqrt{t^2-2t+6}}.
\]
Set this equal to \(\sqrt2\) and square:
\[
(t+2)^2=2(t^2-2t+6),
\]
so \(t^2-8t+8=0\). Thus
\[
\boxed{t=4+2\sqrt2\ \text{or}\ t=4-2\sqrt2}.
\]











注记May/June 2025, Paper 13, Question 5



The plane \(\Pi\) has equation
\[
\mathbf r=2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-2\mathbf k
+m(\mathbf i-2\mathbf j-\mathbf k)
+n(3\mathbf i+2\mathbf j-2\mathbf k).
\]

Find a Cartesian equation of \(\Pi\). [4]

The point \(P\) has position vector \(4\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+9\mathbf k\).

Find the position vector of the foot of the perpendicular from \(P\) to \(\Pi\). [4]

Source: 9231/13/M/J/25 Q5.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
\begin{pmatrix}1\\-2\\-1\end{pmatrix}
\times
\begin{pmatrix}3\\2\\-2\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}6\\-1\\8\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Using \((2,3,-2)\) gives \(d=12-3-16=-7\). Hence
\[
\boxed{6x-y+8z=-7}.
\]

The perpendicular through \(P\) is

\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}4\\2\\9\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}6\\-1\\8\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Substitution in the plane gives
\[
94+101\lambda=-7,
\]
so \(\lambda=-1\). The foot has position vector
\[
\boxed{-2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+\mathbf k}.
\]











注记May/June 2025, Paper 14, Question 3



The points \(A,B,C\) have position vectors
\[
2\mathbf j+3\mathbf k,
\;-5\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+\mathbf k,
\;\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+5\mathbf k.
\]

Find the equation of plane \(ABC\). [5]
Find the perpendicular distance from \(O\) to plane \(ABC\). [2]
Find the acute angle between line \(OA\) and plane \(ABC\). [3]

Source: 9231/14/M/J/25 Q3.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(-5,1,-2),
\;
\overrightarrow{AC}=(1,0,2),
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=(2,8,-1).
\]
Using \(A=(0,2,3)\) gives \(d=13\), so
\[
\boxed{2x+8y-z=13}.
\]



\[
D=\frac{13}{\sqrt{2^2+8^2+(-1)^2}}
=\boxed{\frac{13}{\sqrt{69}}\approx1.57}.
\]

A direction of \(OA\) is \((0,2,3)\). If \(\alpha\) is the angle between the line and the plane, then

\[
\sin\alpha=\frac{|(0,2,3)\boldsymbol\cdot(2,8,-1)|}
{\sqrt{13}\sqrt{69}}
=\frac{13}{\sqrt{897}}.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{\alpha=25.7^\circ}\).











注记October/November 2025, Paper 11/13, Question 5



The plane \(\Pi_1\) has equation
\[
\mathbf r=-3\mathbf i-\mathbf j-\mathbf k
+m(\mathbf j+2\mathbf k)
+n(\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+\mathbf k).
\]

Find an equation of \(\Pi_1\) in Cartesian form. [4]
Find the perpendicular distance from the point with position vector \(-\mathbf i-2\mathbf k\) to \(\Pi_1\). [3]

The plane \(\Pi_2\) has equation \(3x+2y-z=14\).

Find a vector equation of the line of intersection of \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_2\). [4]

Sources: 9231/11/O/N/25 Q5; 9231/13/O/N/25 Q5.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
(0,1,2)\times(1,3,1)=(-5,2,-1),
\]
so take the normal \((5,-2,1)\). Using \((-3,-1,-1)\) gives
\[
\boxed{5x-2y+z=-14}.
\]

For \((-1,0,-2)\),

\[
D=\frac{|5(-1)-2(0)-2+14|}{\sqrt{30}}
=\boxed{\frac7{\sqrt{30}}\approx1.28}.
\]

A direction of the common line is

\[
(5,-2,1)\times(3,2,-1)=(0,8,16)=8(0,1,2).
\]
The point \((0,7,0)\) lies on both planes. Hence
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}0\\7\\0\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\\2\end{pmatrix}}.
\]











注记October/November 2025, Paper 12, Question 6



The plane \(\Pi\) is \(x+3y+2z=1\).

Find the perpendicular distance from \(O\) to \(\Pi\). [2]

Relative to \(O\), the points \(A,B,C\) have position vectors
\[
-\mathbf j+2\mathbf k,
\;2\mathbf i-\mathbf k,
\;2\mathbf i-\mathbf j-\mathbf k.
\]

Find the acute angle between planes \(OAB\) and \(\Pi\). [4]

Source: 9231/12/O/N/25 Q6.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
\boxed{D=\frac1{\sqrt{1^2+3^2+2^2}}=\frac1{\sqrt{14}}}.
\]

A normal to \(OAB\) is

\[
\overrightarrow{OA}\times\overrightarrow{OB}
=(0,-1,2)\times(2,0,-1)=(1,4,2).
\]
The normal to \(\Pi\) is \((1,3,2)\). Therefore
\[
\cos\theta=\frac{|(1,4,2)\boldsymbol\cdot(1,3,2)|}{\sqrt{21}\sqrt{14}}
=\frac{17}{\sqrt{294}}.
\]
Hence \(\boxed{\theta=7.49^\circ}\).











注记October/November 2025, Paper 14, Question 4



The points \(A,B,C\) have position vectors
\[
3\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+5\mathbf k,
\;2\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+2\mathbf k,
\;2\mathbf i+\mathbf j-\mathbf k.
\]

Find the equation of plane \(ABC\). [5]

The point \(D\) has position vector \(\mathbf i-\mathbf j+3\mathbf k\).

Find the shortest distance between lines \(AB\) and \(CD\). [5]

Source: 9231/14/O/N/25 Q4.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(-1,-3,-3),
\;
\overrightarrow{AC}=(-1,-4,-6),
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=(6,-3,1).
\]
Using \(A=(3,5,5)\) gives
\[
\boxed{6x-3y+z=8}.
\]

\(\overrightarrow{CD}=(-1,-2,4)\) and

\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{CD}=(-18,7,-1).
\]
Also \(\overrightarrow{AC}=(-1,-4,-6)\). Thus
\[
D=\frac{|(-1,-4,-6)\boldsymbol\cdot(-18,7,-1)|}{\sqrt{(-18)^2+7^2+(-1)^2}}
=\boxed{\frac4{\sqrt{374}}\approx0.207}.
\]

title: 1.6 Vectors
text:
5. Geometric summary diagrams
以下图形均根据向量关系重新绘制，并以 SVG 直接嵌入页面；虚线表示被遮挡部分或辅助线。




Perpendicular from a point to a plane

Point P, perpendicular foot F and the normal to a plane.  PFnπ


Point-to-plane distance: \(F\) lies on the normal through \(P\).





Intersection of two planes

Two planes meeting in a line, with both normal vectors. π₁π₂n₁n₂l


The intersection direction is parallel to \(\mathbf n_1\times\mathbf n_2\).





Common perpendicular between skew lines

Two skew lines joined by their shortest segment PQ. PQl₁l₂shortest distance


For skew lines, \(PQ\) is parallel to \(\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2\).

title: 1.6 Vectors
text:
6. 完成本节的判断标准

每次先明确 point vector、direction vector 与 normal vector；
判断平行或垂直时能写出对应的 scalar product 条件；
角度题能分清 line-line、line-plane 与 plane-plane 使用的三角函数；
距离题能说明 perpendicular direction 或使用的面积/投影关系；
common perpendicular 和 skew-line distance 能正确使用两个方向向量的 vector product。
